title: "Getting started"

---

End-to-end recipe for economists who already know the LIC-DSF template.

**Edit inputs in Excel.** Change instruments, macro assumptions, stresses, CI,
and realism sheets in the workbook, save, then reload in Python with the load
functions below. Do not construct or mutate loan terms in Python.

## Install

From a local checkout:

```bash
uv sync --all-groups
```

Or as a dependency:

```bash
uv add "lic-dsf @ git+https://github.com/Teal-Insights/py-lic-dsf"
```

Run Python through `uv run` (or a Jupyter kernel from this environment).

## Workbook

Demos use the macros-stripped template: `data/lic-dsf-template-2025-08-12.xlsx`

Point the same loaders at **your filled country workbook** by changing the path. Sheet layout must match the LIC-DSF template generation this library targets (see `data/PROVENANCE.md`).

Template copyright: IMF/World Bank — [`NOTICE.md`](https://github.com/Teal-Insights/py-lic-dsf/blob/main/NOTICE.md).

## Load packages (economist API)

| Function | Loads |
|----------|--------|
| `load_core` | Input 4/5, Ext, Macro → `macro`, `external`, `ext_base`, `pub_base` |
| `load_domestic` | Dom debt inputs |
| `load_stress` | Input 6 + Input 7 ResFin + tailored params |
| `load_rating` | CI Summary, triggers, Input 1 market |
| `load_realism` | Imported data + Realism assumptions |
| `load_probability` | Distress covariates (Output 6) |

Day-1 needs only `load_core`. Typical DSA notebooks add `load_stress` and
`load_rating`.

## Minimal script: Output 1-1 / 1-2

```python
from pathlib import Path

from lic_dsf.load import load_core
from lic_dsf.output import external_dsa_panel, public_dsa_panel

workbook = Path("data/lic-dsf-template-2025-08-12.xlsx")
macro, external, ext_base, pub_base = load_core(workbook)

out_1_1 = external_dsa_panel(ext_base)  # Output 1-1 shape
out_1_2 = public_dsa_panel(pub_base)  # Output 1-2 shape
```

## Export panels to a spreadsheet

To write Output 1–7 (plus Summary / Database) panels into a **new** sidecar
workbook — without overwriting the official template:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from lic_dsf.export import to_workbook_from_path

to_workbook_from_path(
    Path("data/lic-dsf-template-2025-08-12.xlsx"),
    Path("outputs/panels.xlsx"),
)
```

`lic_dsf.run.compute_outputs` builds the DataFrames; `lic_dsf.export.to_workbook`
writes them. Pass `include={...}` to compute a subset of sheet titles (see
`lic_dsf.run.OUTPUT_SHEET_ORDER`).

Quick stress sketch after `load_core`:

```python
from lic_dsf.load import load_stress
from lic_dsf.output import stress_external_panel
from lic_dsf.stress import run_b1_gdp_external

stress = load_stress(workbook)
stressed = run_b1_gdp_external(macro, external, stress.input6, stress.residual)
stress_external_panel(stressed)
```

## Caveats

- **Excel fidelity.** Numerics aim to match the Excel engine; treat unexpected
  differences as bugs unless a doc/demo notes an intentional approximation
  (e.g. some public stress GFN / ResFin feedback).
- **Your workbook.** Loaders expect the official sheet structure. Renamed sheets
  or older template vintages may fail or misalign years.
- **Not a replacement UI.** Official chart chrome, i18n labels, and VBA macros
  are out of scope. Use `lic_dsf.export.to_workbook` for a panel-style sidecar
  `.xlsx` of Outputs 1–7.
- **License.** MIT for code; do not redistribute the template beyond the terms
  in `NOTICE.md`.

## Jupyter

```bash
uv run jupyter notebook demo/baseline_dsa.ipynb
```

Each demo resolves `REPO_ROOT` whether you start from the repo root or `demo/`.
